title: Construction of Large Cranial Windows for Long-term Two-Photon Imaging in Mice
author: Taiga Takahashi
license_note: PMC full-text XML — Bio-protocol — CC-BY confirmed in article XML

steps.title: Prepare fabrication solutions
steps.instruction: Make the three solutions needed for the PEO‑CYTOP nanosheet: (1) dissolve CYTOP in perfluorotributylamine to 30 mg mL⁻¹ (0.5 mL for a 40 × 40 mm² sheet); (2) dissolve PVA (MW 22 000) in distilled water to 10 mg mL⁻¹ using the same volume as the CYTOP solution; (3) mix Sylgard 184 base and curing agent 10:1 (w/w), stir a few minutes at room temperature, then dilute to 1.25 wt% in hexane, store sealed at 4 °C and use within one week (handle hexane in a fume hood with nitrile gloves).

steps.title: Spin‑coat PVA sacrificial layer
steps.instruction: Apply the PVA solution onto a silicon wafer (200 nm SiO₂, cut into the desired square size) with a glass dropper, then spin‑coat at 4,000 rpm for 20 s; wait 2–3 min before the next coating.

steps.title: Spin‑coat CYTOP layer
steps.instruction: Dispense the CYTOP solution onto the PVA‑coated wafer and spin‑coat at 4,000 rpm for 60 s; wait 2–3 min before the next step.

steps.title: Spin‑coat silicone layer
steps.instruction: Apply the silicone (PDMS) solution onto the CYTOP‑coated wafer and spin‑coat at 4,000 rpm for 20 s at room temperature; wait 2–3 min.

steps.title: Cure multilayer composite
steps.instruction: Place the coated wafer in an oven at 80 °C for 2 h.

steps.title: Oxygen plasma treatment
steps.instruction: Treat the cured composite with oxygen plasma at 11 W (medium power) for 60 s to increase surface hydrophilicity.

steps.title: Prepare PEO‑silane solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 2‑(methoxy(polyethyleneoxy)propyl)trichlorosilane to 2 mM in toluene inside a Teflon Petri dish (ϕ 150 mm, height 30 mm, capacity 300 mL); 100 mL is sufficient for four 40 × 40 mm² sheets. Prepare immediately before use.

steps.title: Silanize substrate
steps.instruction: Submerge the coated wafer fully in the PEO‑silane solution for 1 h; ensure complete immersion.

steps.title: Release nanosheet from wafer
steps.instruction: Immerse the silanized wafer in water to dissolve the PVA sacrificial layer; the PEO‑CYTOP nanosheet will detach and float on the water surface.

steps.title: Transfer nanosheet to fabric
steps.instruction: Using tweezers, pick up the floating nanosheet (hydrophilic side outward) and place it onto a sterilized nonwoven fabric (UV‑sterilized 8 W for 30 min). Verify hydrophilicity by a spreading water droplet.

steps.title: Dry nanosheet
steps.instruction: Allow the nanosheet on the fabric to dry overnight (minimum 12 h) at room temperature; store the dried sheet in a dry, dust‑free container.

steps.title: Fabricate head plate
steps.instruction: Machine a 1‑mm‑thick aluminum plate into the head plate shape shown in Figure 1.

steps.title: Assemble UV irradiator
steps.instruction: Build the programmable UV‑LED system by connecting an LED control board, UV‑LED, board case, and glass diffuser; mount the assembly on a metal arm with a magnetic base as illustrated in Figure 2.

steps.title: Sterilize surgical tools
steps.instruction: Soak scalpel, scissors, tweezers, drill bit, head plate, and head holder in 70 % ethanol.

steps.title: Prepare drug syringes
steps.instruction: Load GLYCEOL injection (15 µL g⁻¹ body weight) into one syringe and 200 µL of 2 % xylocaine into a second syringe.

steps.title: Anesthetize mouse
steps.instruction: Induce anesthesia with isoflurane at 3 % using an inhalation system; maintain at 1.5 % throughout the procedure.

steps.title: Prepare scalp and eyes
steps.instruction: Disinfect scalp hair with 70 % ethanol‑soaked cotton swabs, apply ophthalmic ointment to the eyes, then shave the hair and wipe remaining hair with ethanol‑soaked swabs.

steps.title: Secure mouse in frame
steps.instruction: Place the anesthetized mouse in a stereotaxic frame.

steps.title: Apply local anesthetic (first dose)
steps.instruction: Drop a few µL of xylocaine onto the skin, wait 3 min.

steps.title: Incise skin over skull
steps.instruction: Cut the skin with surgical scissors to expose the dorsal skull (parietal, frontal, temporal, occipital regions).

steps.title: Apply local anesthetic (second dose)
steps.instruction: Place additional xylocaine drops on the exposed skull and wait 3 min.

steps.title: Remove periosteum
steps.instruction: Carefully peel off the periosteum from the skull surface using a scalpel or forceps; ensure complete removal.

steps.title: Separate temporal and occipital muscles
steps.instruction: Detach these muscles from the skull with fine forceps.

steps.title: Attach head plate
steps.instruction: Align the head plate parallel to the transverse plane of the skull, secure it with dental resin, and allow the resin to cure for 15 min.

steps.title: Inject GLYCEOL
steps.instruction: Administer GLYCEOL intraperitoneally at 15 µL g⁻¹ body weight to lower intracranial pressure.

steps.title: Drill and thin skull
steps.instruction: Create a groove around the intended craniotomy with a drill bit, then gradually thin the bone until it can be depressed with tweezers; use a horizontal circular motion and avoid vertical pressure.

steps.title: Remove skull piece
steps.instruction: Soak the drilled groove with saline, insert tweezers parallel to the brain surface, and gently lift the skull while keeping it wet with saline.

steps.title: Achieve hemostasis
steps.instruction: Press a saline‑soaked Spongel against any bleeding site with forceps until bleeding stops.

steps.title: Trim nanosheet and fabric
steps.instruction: Cut the PEO‑CYTOP nanosheet and the supporting nonwoven fabric with scissors to match the exposed brain area; keep the sheet slightly oversized initially to estimate size, then trim to fit.

steps.title: Prepare brain surface
steps.instruction: Apply a few drops of saline to the brain, then remove excess fluid with a paper towel or suction pump.

steps.title: Place nanosheet on brain
steps.instruction: Position the nanosheet with the hydrophilic side facing the brain, gently press it onto the surface using tweezers over the nonwoven fabric; avoid excessive pressure.

steps.title: Remove supporting fabric
steps.instruction: Peel off the nonwoven fabric from the nanosheet with tweezers.

steps.title: Trim nanosheet edge
steps.instruction: Trim the nanosheet edge a few millimeters away from the exposed brain using tweezers.

steps.title: Glue nanosheet edges
steps.instruction: Apply Aron Alpha gel to the nanosheet edges and the skull surface; if brain swelling occurs, give an additional GLYCEOL injection (5 µL g⁻¹) before fixation.

steps.title: Apply dental resin barrier
steps.instruction: Cover the glued area with dental resin (Unifast II or Ionosit baseliner) to create a barrier for the forthcoming light‑curable resin.

steps.title: Apply light‑curable resin
steps.instruction: Discard a few drops of the resin elsewhere to avoid bubbles, then drop the resin onto the nanosheet covering the window.

steps.title: UV cure resin
steps.instruction: Irradiate with the UV‑LED system using the following pattern: 365 nm, 10 mW, 2 s every 30 s for 3 min, then 10 s every 30 s for 7 min (adjust pattern for other resins). Use intermittent exposure to limit temperature rise.

steps.title: Protect cranial window
steps.instruction: Place utility wax (GC) around the window edge, lay a silicone‑coated mixing paper (CG No.1) on the wax, and secure with vinyl tape; avoid contact of wax or paper with the window surface.

steps.title: Clean surface if needed
steps.instruction: If debris appears, remove it with an air duster or by applying water and suction; for stubborn particles, gently wipe with a moist cotton swab the day after the experiment.
